One synthetic FC65 tag with short ID 4660 and an incrementing three-byte field. Local RSSI is measured by the receiving device.
A six-byte transmitter identity with reported RSSI from -95 to -40. This value is payload content; it does not set the signal measured from this phone.
Two explicit radio pauses and 15% deterministic omissions. This percentage is a scenario setting, not measured packet loss.
Two alternating tracks: a 24-bit wrap and a 16-bit wrap with reset after 20 attempts. A counter gap alone does not establish radio loss.
A 24-bit field crosses from 0x05FFFF to 0x060000. The experimental decoder changes its candidate interpretation here; temperature remains unconfirmed.
06 · Two tracks sharing a short ID
Both virtual tracks use ID 4660 with different counter sequences. They share one phone radio and are not independent physical Bluetooth transmitters.
Cycles through empty, truncated, status and unknown FC65 payloads. BLE carries intentionally incomplete or unknown application data.
An increasing reported RSSI with sentinel 127 every fifth attempt. The receiving chart must distinguish unavailable values from strong reception.
Direct and relayed records, arrival/departure, pauses, omissions and a sentinel. Tracks share one radio; the seed and profile reproduce the planned bytes.

Advertises only the synthetic name VESPA-NANO-SIM, without manufacturer data, service UUIDs or telemetry. The guarded name workflow temporarily changes the phone Bluetooth name and restores it after stopping. Hardware compatibility is unverified.

Synthetic name vn0CqrvM3e7/ encodes logical identity AA:BB:CC:DD:EE:FF and parameter 0C, whose hardware meaning is unknown. Local Name only, without manufacturer data or GATT. The receiver measures RSSI. The phone name is temporarily changed and restored; its radio address is not selected.

Synthetic name-encoded tag. Logical identity %1$s, PP %2$s (hardware meaning unknown), advertised name %3$s. Local Name only; no manufacturer data or GATT. The receiver measures RSSI. Hardware compatibility is unverified.
